script: セイバールート四日目-00
title: セイバールート四日目-00

pages.ja: それは、五年前の冬の話。
pages.jaRuby: それは、五年前の冬の話。
pages.en: It happened one winter, five years ago.
pages.mirrorMoon: This is a story from a winter five years ago.

pages.ja:
月の綺麗な夜だった。
自分は何をするでもなく、父である衛宮切嗣と月見をしている。
冬だというのに、気温はそう低くはなかった。
縁側はわずかに肌寒いだけで、月を肴にするにはいい夜だった。
pages.jaRuby:
月の綺麗な夜だった。
自分は何をするでもなく、父である衛宮切嗣と月見をしている。
冬だというのに、気温はそう低くはなかった。
縁側はわずかに肌寒いだけで、月を肴にするにはいい夜だった。
pages.en:
The moon was beautiful that night.

I was doing nothing in particular, merely sitting with my father, Kiritsugu Emiya, and looking up at it.

Despite the season, the night was not terribly cold.

There was only a faint chill on the veranda. It was a good night to sit with the moon for company.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It was a night with a beautiful moon.
I wasn’t doing anything, just watching the moon with Kiritsugu.
Even though it was winter, the weather wasn’t cold.
The corridor was only a little chilly, and it was a good night to enjoy the moon.

pages.ja:
この頃、切嗣は外出が少なくなっていた。
あまり外に出ず、家にこもってのんびりとしている事が多くなった。
……今でも、思い出せば後悔する。
それが死期を悟った動物に似ていたのだと、どうして気が付かなかったのか。
pages.jaRuby:
この頃、切嗣は外出が少なくなっていた。
あまり外に出ず、家にこもってのんびりとしている事が多くなった。
……今でも、思い出せば後悔する。
それが死期を悟った動物に似ていたのだと、どうして気が付かなかったのか。
pages.en:
By then, Kiritsugu had stopped going out as often.

He rarely left the house. More and more, he remained at home and passed the days in peace.

…Even now, the memory fills me with regret.

Why did I never realize that he resembled an animal that knows its death is near?
pages.mirrorMoon:
Back then, Kiritsugu didn’t leave the house much.
Not going outside, he would just laze carelessly around the house.
…I regret it even now, thinking back to it.
Why didn’t I notice that it was like the actions of an animal that knows its time of death?

pages.ja:
「子供の頃、僕は正義の味方に憧れてた」
ふと。
自分から見たら正義の味方そのものの父は、懐かしむように、そんな事を呟いた。
pages.jaRuby:
「子供の頃、僕は正義の味方に憧れてた」
ふと。
自分から見たら正義の味方そのものの父は、懐かしむように、そんな事を呟いた。
pages.en:
“When I was a child, I wanted to become a Hero of Justice.”

Without warning,

my father—who had always seemed the very image of a Hero of Justice to me—murmured those words with nostalgia.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“When I was a child, I wanted to be a superhero.”
Suddenly.
That man, himself a superhero in my child’s eyes, said that as if yearning for it.

pages.ja:
「なんだよそれ。憧れてたって、諦めたのかよ」
むっとして言い返す。
切嗣はすまなそうに笑って、遠い月を仰いだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「なんだよそれ。憧れてたって、諦めたのかよ」
むっとして言い返す。
切嗣はすまなそうに笑って、遠い月を仰いだ。
pages.en:
“What's that supposed to mean? You *wanted* to? Did you give up?”

I bristled as I answered.

Kiritsugu smiled apologetically and raised his eyes toward the distant moon.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“What? What do you mean by ‘wanted’? Did you give up?”
I became angry and asked him.
Kiritsugu laughed apologetically and looked up at the sky.

pages.ja:
「うん、残念ながらね。ヒーローは期間限定で、オトナになると名乗るのが難しくなるんだ。そんなコト、もっと早くに気が付けば良かった」
言われて納得した。
なんでそうなのかは分からなかったが、切嗣の言うことだから間違いないと思ったのだ。
pages.jaRuby:
「うん、残念ながらね。ヒーローは期間限定で、オトナになると名乗るのが難しくなるんだ。そんなコト、もっと早くに気が付けば良かった」
言われて納得した。
なんでそうなのかは分からなかったが、切嗣の言うことだから間違いないと思ったのだ。
pages.en:
“Yes, I'm afraid so. Being a hero is for a limited time. Once you grow up, it becomes difficult to call yourself one. I wish I'd realized that sooner.”

His answer made sense to me.

I did not understand *why* it was true, but Kiritsugu had said it, and I believed he could not be wrong.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yes, unfortunately. Being a hero is a time-limited thing, and it becomes hard to call yourself that when you grow up. I wish I’d found that out earlier.”
I agreed with that.
I didn’t know why, but I thought it couldn’t be wrong because Kiritsugu said so.

pages.ja:
「そっか。それじゃしょうがないな」
「そうだね。本当に、しょうがない」
相づちをうつ切嗣。
だから当然、俺の台詞なんて決まっていた。
pages.jaRuby:
「そっか。それじゃしょうがないな」
「そうだね。本当に、しょうがない」
相づちをうつ切嗣。
だから当然、俺の台詞なんて決まっていた。
pages.en:
“I see. Then I suppose we have no choice.”

“Yeah. There’s nothing else we can do.”

Kiritsugu agrees.

And so, naturally, there is only one thing I can say.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“I see. Then I guess it couldn’t be helped.”
“Yeah. It really couldn’t be helped.”
Kiritsugu answers.
So of course, my response was determined.

pages.ja:
「うん、しょうがないから俺が代わりになってやるよ。
爺さんはオトナだからもう無理だけど、俺なら大丈夫だろ。まかせろって、爺さんの夢は」
pages.jaRuby:
「うん、しょうがないから俺が代わりになってやるよ。
爺さんはオトナだからもう無理だけど、俺なら大丈夫だろ。まかせろって、爺さんの夢は」
pages.en:
“Then I'll take your place. You're a grown-up now, old man, so it's too late for you. But I can still do it.

“Leave your dream to me—”
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Yeah, it can’t be helped, so I’ll take your place.
It’s impossible since you’re an adult, but it should be all right for me. Let me take on your dream.

pages.ja:
“
俺が、ちゃんと形にしてやるから”
pages.jaRuby:
“
俺が、ちゃんと形にしてやるから”
pages.en: *I’ll make it real for you.*
pages.mirrorMoon: ‘I’ll make it come true.’

pages.ja:
そう言い切る前に、父は微笑った。
続きなんて聞くまでもないっていう顔だった。
衛宮切嗣はそうか、と長く息を吸って、
「ああ
安心した」
静かに目蓋を閉じて、その人生を終えていた。
pages.jaRuby:
そう言い切る前に、父は[ruby text=わら o2o=1]微笑った。
続きなんて聞くまでもないっていう顔だった。
衛宮切嗣はそうか、と長く息を吸って、

安心した」

pages.en:
Before I can finish saying it, my father smiles.

His expression tells me there is no need to hear the rest.

“I see.”

Kiritsugu Emiya draws one long breath.

“Ah—what a relief.”

Then he quietly closes his eyes and brings his life to an end.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Before I could finish, my father laughed.
He made a face like he didn’t even need to hear the rest.
After breathing in, Emiya Kiritsugu said…
“YeahI’m relieved.”
He quietly closed his eyes and his life ended.

pages.ja:
それが、朝になれば目覚めるような穏やかさだったから、幼い自分は騒ぎ立てなかった。
死というものを見慣れていた事もあったのだろう。
何をするでもなく、冬の月と、長い眠りに入った、父親だった人を見上げていた。
pages.jaRuby:
それが、朝になれば目覚めるような穏やかさだったから、幼い自分は騒ぎ立てなかった。
死というものを見慣れていた事もあったのだろう。
何をするでもなく、冬の月と、長い眠りに入った、父親だった人を見上げていた。
pages.en:
He died with the same peace as someone falling asleep, certain they would wake in the morning. The child I was did not raise an alarm.

Perhaps I had simply seen death too many times.

I did nothing. I looked up at the winter moon and at the man who had been my father, now entered into a long sleep.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Since he looked so peaceful, I thought he would wake up again in the morning, so I didn’t disturb him.
Perhaps being used to seeing death factored in too.
Without doing anything, I just looked up at the man who was my father, as he entered a long sleep.

pages.ja:
庭には虫の声もなく、あたりは静かだった。
明るい夜の中、両目だけが熱かったのを覚えている。
泣き声もあげず、悲しいと思う事もない。
月が落ちるまで、ただ、涙だけが止まらなかった。
pages.jaRuby:
庭には虫の声もなく、あたりは静かだった。
明るい[ruby text=やみ]夜の中、両目だけが熱かったのを覚えている。
泣き声もあげず、悲しいと思う事もない。
月が落ちるまで、ただ、涙だけが止まらなかった。
pages.en:
No insects called in the garden. Everything around us was silent.

In that brilliant night—that luminous darkness—I remember that only my eyes felt hot.

I did not sob. I did not even feel sad.

Until the moon sank, only the tears refused to stop.
pages.mirrorMoon:
There were no sounds of insects in the garden as it was silent.
In the bright night, I remember only my eyes being hot.
I did not cry out nor did I feel sad.
But I could not stop my tears until the moon sank.

pages.ja:
それが五年前の冬の話。
むこう十年分ぐらい泣いたおかげか、その後はサッパリしたものだった。
pages.jaRuby:
それが五年前の冬の話。
むこう十年分ぐらい泣いたおかげか、その後はサッパリしたものだった。
pages.en:
That happened one winter, five years ago.

Perhaps I cried enough that night to last the next ten years. Afterward, I felt remarkably clear.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That is the story from a winter five years ago.
Perhaps I cried ten years worth of tears since after that, there was nothing.

pages.ja:
藤ねえの親父さんに葬儀の段取りをしてもらって、衛宮の屋敷に一人で住むようになった。
切嗣がいなくなっても変わらない。
衛宮士郎は切嗣のような正義の味方になるのだから、のんびりしている暇などありはしない。
pages.jaRuby:
藤ねえの親父さんに葬儀の段取りをしてもらって、衛宮の屋敷に一人で住むようになった。
切嗣がいなくなっても変わらない。
衛宮士郎は[ruby text=オヤジ char=2]切嗣のような正義の味方になるのだから、のんびりしている暇などありはしない。
pages.en:
Fuji's father arranged the funeral, and I began living alone in the Emiya house.

Nothing changed when Kiritsugu disappeared.

Shirou Emiya intended to become a Hero of Justice like Dad. There was no time to idle.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Fuji-nee’s father planned the funeral, and I started living in this house by myself.
Nothing changed even though Kiritsugu was gone.
Emiya Shirou would become a superhero like Emiya Kiritsugu, so there was no time to be playing around.

pages.ja:
そう。
口にはしなかったけど、ちゃんと覚えていたんだ。
十年前、火事場に残されていた自分を救い出してくれた男の姿を。
意識もなく、全身に火傷を負って死にかけていた子供を抱き上げて、目に涙をためるぐらい喜んで、外に連れ出してくれた。
pages.jaRuby:
そう。
口にはしなかったけど、ちゃんと覚えていたんだ。
十年前、火事場に残されていた自分を救い出してくれた男の姿を。
意識もなく、全身に火傷を負って死にかけていた子供を抱き上げて、目に涙をためるぐらい喜んで、外に連れ出してくれた。
pages.en:
—Yes.

I never spoke of it, but I remembered perfectly.

I remembered the man who rescued me when I was left behind in the fire ten years ago.

He lifted a dying child from the flames—unconscious, burned over his whole body—and carried him outside with tears of joy in his eyes.
pages.mirrorMoon:
That’s right.
I didn’t mention it, but I remember perfectly.
The figure of the man who saved me, who was left to the fire ten years ago.
He held up in his arms an unconscious child, about to die from burns. He became so happy that tears welled up in his eyes, and took the child outside.

pages.ja:
その時から、彼は俺の憧れになった。
誰も助けてくれなかった。
誰も助けてやれなかった。
その中でただ一人助けられた自分と、ただ一人助けてくれた人がいた。
だから、そういう人間になろうと思ったのだ。
pages.jaRuby:
その時から、彼は俺の憧れになった。
誰も助けてくれなかった。
誰も助けてやれなかった。
その中でただ一人助けられた自分と、ただ一人助けてくれた人がいた。
だから、そういう人間になろうと思ったのだ。
pages.en:
From that moment, he became the person I admired.

No one came to save me.

I couldn't save anyone.

Amid all of that, there was one person who was saved, and one person alone who saved him.

—That was why I decided to become someone like him.
pages.mirrorMoon:
From that time, he was the subject of my admiration.
No one saved me.
I couldn’t save anyone.
In it all, I was saved, and a person was there to save me.
That’s why I decided to become like him.

pages.ja:
彼のように誰かを助けて、誰も死なせないようにする正義の味方に。
その彼こそが“そういうモノ”に成りたかったと遺して、自分の前で穏やかに幕を閉じた。
pages.jaRuby:
彼のように誰かを助けて、誰も死なせないようにする正義の味方に。
その彼こそが“そういうモノ”に成りたかったと遺して、自分の前で穏やかに幕を閉じた。
pages.en:
A Hero of Justice who would save people as he had, who would allow no one to die.

Then that man left behind the confession that he, too, had wanted to become *such a thing*, and quietly lowered the curtain before my eyes.
pages.mirrorMoon:
Become a superhero, so that I could save people and let no one be killed… just like him.
Kiritsugu died peacefully, leaving me his dream of becoming a superhero himself.

pages.ja:
子が父の跡を継ぐのは当然のこと。
衛宮士郎は正義の味方になって、かつての自分のような誰かを助けなくてはいけない。
幼い頃にそう誓った。
誰よりも憧れたあの男の代わりに、彼の夢を果たすのだと。
pages.jaRuby:
子が父の跡を継ぐのは当然のこと。
衛宮士郎は正義の味方になって、かつての自分のような誰かを助けなくてはいけない。
幼い頃にそう誓った。
誰よりも憧れたあの男の代わりに、彼の夢を果たすのだと。
pages.en:
It is only natural for a child to carry on his father's work.

Shirou Emiya has to become a Hero of Justice and save someone like the boy he once was.

I swore it as a child.

In place of the man I admired above all others, I would fulfill his dream.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It’s only natural for a child to succeed their father.
Emiya Shirou must become a superhero and save someone just like the old me.
I swore so as a child.
To fulfill the dream of the man I admired the most.

切嗣の言っていた正義の味方ってどんなモノなのかとか、早く一人前になる方法とか、切嗣の口癖だったみんなが幸せでいられればいい、なんて魔法みたいな夢の実現方法とか、それと、マスターなんてモノになっちまって、一緒に付いてきた金髪の女の子とか頭んなかがゴチャゴチャだ、ホント

pages.en:
…Though honestly, I understand very little.

What sort of thing Kiritsugu meant by a Hero of Justice, how I am supposed to become a full-fledged mage anytime soon, how anyone could realize that impossible dream he always spoke of where everybody gets to be happy, and now I have somehow become something called a Master and there is a blond girl following me around and my head is a complete mess, honestly—
pages.mirrorMoon:
…But honestly, I don’t get it.
What this superhero thing is supposed to be, how to become one, how to make everyone happy like Kiritsugu always said… and I became this thing called a Master and things like the blond-haired girl following me around is confusing my head and really

目を覚ますと見慣れた部屋にいた。
「……う……口ん中、まずい……」
濁った血の味がする。
口内に血が溜まっていたのか、呼吸をするだけでどろっとした空気が流れ込んできた。

pages.en:
“………”

I open my eyes in my familiar room.

“…Ugh… My mouth tastes awful…”

The taste is of old, stagnant blood.

Perhaps blood pooled inside my mouth as I slept. Every breath draws in thick, clotted air.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“……!”
When I open my eyes, I’m in a familiar room.
“What, I’m in my own room?”
As soon as I speak, I start to feel terribly sick.
“…Ugh… it tastes bad… in my mouth…”
I taste blood in my mouth.
Maybe it was filling my mouth, but I breathe in thick air.

“………”

I open my eyes in my familiar room.

“What? This is my room.”

The moment I speak, a violent wave of sickness comes over me.

“…Ugh… My mouth tastes awful…”

The taste is of old, stagnant blood.

Perhaps blood pooled inside my mouth as I slept. Every breath draws in thick, clotted air.

“—”

I have no idea how I ended up like this.

But the nausea is overwhelming. For now, I want to reach the washroom and splash water on my face.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“”
I’m not sure why I feel like this.
I feel really sick to my stomach, so I want to go to the bathroom and wash my face.

pages.en:
“—Hup.”

I sit up.

The room spins.

I nearly collapse and catch myself against the wall.

“…Ugh.”

Movement worsens the nausea.

…No. This is closer to agony than nausea.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“All right.”
I stand up.
I feel dizzy.
I almost fall and support myself by putting a hand against the wall.
“…Ugh.”
The nausea increases when I move.
…No, this is more like pain than nausea.

pages.ja:
体は重いし、動く度に腹ん中がぐるんぐるんと回るよう。きっと胃に焼けた鉛を流し込んだら、こんな気分になるのではないだろうか。
「……あつ……ヘンな想像したら熱でてきた」
額に滲んだ汗を拭って、よたよたと壁づたいに部屋を出る。

pages.en:
My body feels leaden, and every movement sends my insides churning. If someone poured molten lead into my stomach, I imagine it would feel much like this.

“…Hot… I imagined it too vividly, and now I'm running a fever.”

I wipe the sweat from my forehead and stagger out of the room with one hand against the wall.
pages.mirrorMoon:
My body is heavy and it feels like my stomach is turning every time I move. Maybe someone would feel like this if someone poured burning lead into their stomach.
“…Ugh… Imagining that is giving me headaches.”
I wipe the sweat off my forehead and wobble out of my room.

pages.ja:
「……よし、少しは落ち着いた」
顔を洗って、ついでに汗ばんでいた体を拭く。
「……？」
なぜか腹には包帯が巻かれていた。

“…?”

I cannot imagine why, so I set the question aside for now.

pages.mirrorMoon:
“…I’m hungry. I wonder if there are any leftovers…”
Even though my stomach feels terrible, my body wants energy.

いたたた
」

“Ngh…”

I steel myself and begin edging along the wall.

The dizziness has not improved, and more than anything, my body feels slow.

“Ow—ow, ow…”

I advance with a pathetic whimper.

…What on earth did I do before going to sleep?

I certainly do not remember training hard enough to leave every muscle in my body aching.
pages.mirrorMoon:
“Guh…”
Putting my mind into it, I start to walk along the wall.
I still feel dizzy, and my body feels dull.
“OwOwww”
I walk forward, letting out miserable sounds.
…Really, what did I do before going to bed?
I don’t remember any training that could have caused this pain.
